key_insight: DynaWeb learns a compact world model of the web so LLM-based agents can train via imagined interactions (Dyna-style), dramatically reducing costly, risky live-web exploration while enabling effective policy learning.
problem_solved: Addresses the inefficiency, cost, and safety risks of training autonomous web agents by replacing large amounts of live internet interaction with model-guided simulated experience.
method: Train a learned world model that predicts web state transitions and outcomes (DOM changes, responses, tool calls) from limited real interactions and logs.
Use the world model to generate imagined rollouts and perform planning/updates (Dyna-style) to train LLM-driven policies with far fewer real-environment steps.
Iteratively validate and correct model bias with selective real-world interaction to maintain robustness and safety.
impact: Makes development of autonomous web agents more sample-efficient, safer, and cost-effective, enabling practitioners to train scalable LLM-based assistants that navigate and act on the web with far fewer live queries.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: world model + imagined rollouts + policy/LLM, with arrows showing training loop
Training loop flowchart: real data → model learning → simulated rollouts → policy update → selective real validation
Bar/chart illustrating sample-efficiency: real interactions required (baseline) vs DynaWeb (reduced)
Task storyboard: example web task (search, click, form-fill) showing imagined vs real execution
paper_title: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents
paper_authors: Hang Ding, Peidong Liu, Junqiao Wang, Ziwei Ji, Meng Cao
